The sequence increases by **63** for most terms. At specific positions (7, 13, 18, 22, ...), there are **larger increases** forming an arithmetic sequence (350, 413, 476, ...). The recursive definition incorporates these special increases at the calculated positions. 

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{For } n \geq 1: \\
&a(n) = 
\begin{cases}
a(n-1) + 63 + 350 + 63(k-1) & \text{if } n = 7 + \frac{(k-1)(14 - k)}{2} \text{ for some } k \\
a(n-1) + 63 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
}
$$
